title: Hyderabad's Uday Ruddarraju Named OpenAI's CTO of Compute
excerpt: The CBIT Hyderabad graduate, who previously built infrastructure at xAI and Robinhood, will oversee the massive computing backbone powering GPT-5.6 and future frontier models.
body:
• OpenAI has promoted Hyderabad-born engineer Uday Ruddarraju to Chief Technology Officer of Compute, one of the company's most strategically important roles.
  • Ruddarraju joined OpenAI in July 2025 from Elon Musk's xAI, where he helped build the Colossus supercomputer cluster with over 200,000 GPUs.
  • As CTO of Compute, he oversees the infrastructure — networking, storage, and ML systems — behind training frontier models including GPT-5.6.
  • A graduate of Chaitanya Bharathi Institute of Technology (CBIT) in Hyderabad, he holds an MS in Computer Science from the University of Minnesota.

OpenAI has elevated Indian-origin engineer Uday Ruddarraju to Chief Technology Officer of Compute, placing a Hyderabad-born infrastructure specialist at the helm of one of artificial intelligence's most consequential engineering challenges: keeping the computing power behind ChatGPT and its successors growing fast enough to match the company's ambitions.

The promotion, announced on July 20 via LinkedIn, comes almost exactly a year after Ruddarraju joined OpenAI from Elon Musk's rival AI venture xAI. At OpenAI, the role of CTO of Compute may lack the public profile of CEO Sam Altman, but insiders regard it as among the most strategically vital positions in the organisation.

From Hyderabad Classrooms to Silicon Valley's AI Frontier

Ruddarraju's path to one of the most watched jobs in AI began at Chaitanya Bharathi Institute of Technology (CBIT), a private engineering college in Hyderabad, where he studied computer science. He interned at Amazon Web Services while still an undergraduate before moving to the United States for a Master's degree in Computer Science at the University of Minnesota.

His professional career reads like a tour through Silicon Valley's infrastructure elite. From 2013 to 2018, he worked at eBay, helping modernise its cloud infrastructure and driving Kubernetes adoption across the company's vast server fleet. He then joined Robinhood as Senior Director of Engineering and Head of Infrastructure, leading a team of 160 engineers as the trading platform scaled from one million to 24 million users.

In 2024, Ruddarraju took on the role of Head of Infrastructure Engineering at xAI, overseeing compute, networking, storage, and data centres. There, he helped build the Colossus supercomputer — a cluster of more than 200,000 GPUs that became one of the largest AI training systems in the world.

Scaling OpenAI's Compute Ambitions

As CTO of Compute, Ruddarraju's mandate goes well beyond procuring chips. He oversees the software platforms, networking architecture, storage systems, and operational frameworks that enable OpenAI to train increasingly powerful models while serving hundreds of millions of users worldwide.

"Our Compute team has worked relentlessly to bring capacity online quickly and reliably, while doing the deep systems across compute, network and storage, and ML work needed to train frontier models like GPT-5.6. As we scale, the problems only get harder — requiring pushing the frontiers and innovating across every layer of the stack."

— Uday Ruddarraju, CTO of Compute, OpenAI

The appointment reflects a broader shift in the AI industry. For years, breakthroughs were driven primarily by algorithmic advances. Today, raw computing power has become the principal constraint and strategic differentiator. Companies are pouring tens of billions of dollars into data centres, specialised chips, and energy infrastructure. OpenAI itself has committed to a massive expansion of its computing footprint, with cloud and infrastructure spending measured in the hundreds of billions of dollars.

Ruddarraju signalled that OpenAI's infrastructure buildout is far from over. He said the company is hiring across distributed systems, hardware engineering, manufacturing, and data centre construction — spanning civil, mechanical, and electrical engineering disciplines.

Another Indian-Origin Leader at AI's Core

Ruddarraju's elevation adds to the growing roster of Indian-origin executives shaping the global technology landscape. From Satya Nadella at Microsoft to Sundar Pichai at Google, Indian-born leaders have long helmed the world's largest tech companies. A newer generation is now building the foundational infrastructure of the AI era itself.

For India's technology talent pipeline, particularly graduates from the country's private engineering colleges, Ruddarraju's trajectory — from a Hyderabad campus to the executive suite at the world's most prominent AI company — underscores the global demand for deep infrastructure expertise, not just algorithmic research.

"We're on a mission to build the world's largest compute footprint so frontier AI can reach everyone and every workflow."

— Uday Ruddarraju, CTO of Compute, OpenAI

As AI models grow larger and more capable, the engineers building the systems that train and deploy them will increasingly determine who leads the race. In that contest, Ruddarraju now holds one of the most important seats at the table.
